$comment: A nominal brand over `string`: CEL types a host path as `Telo.HostPath`, so `+` does not quietly turn one into a plain string and a plain string is not accepted where one is required. It is extended with `.joinPath(relative)` and read as text with `string(path)`. `fromHost` names the anchor a host-supplied value (an env var, or the `default:` standing in for one) is resolved against; every other value of this type must already be absolute. The `entry` parameter is found by its `hostEntry` flag, never by its name: its argument is a token (`file` | `directory`) saying what the path names when something is there, each runtime mapping it to its own filesystem query. The `mediaType` parameter is found by its `hostMediaType` flag: its argument is a key of its `signatures`, each a list of alternative hex patterns read from the file's first byte (`??` any byte).
name: Telo.HostPath

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: What the path names when something is there: `directory`, or `file` (anything that is not a directory; links are followed). Omitted means either. An absent path is never refused by it — a database file or a journal directory is created by whatever uses it.

parameters.name: mediaType
parameters.description: The media type of the file the path names, judged by its leading bytes: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp` or `application/pdf`. A directory there does not hold one. Omitted means any. An absent path is never refused by it.

description: An absolute path on the machine running the application — a data directory, a database file, an output location. A variable of this type set from the environment may be relative and is resolved against the working directory; anywhere else a relative path is refused. Extend one with `.joinPath('sub/dir')`, which uses the host's separator. A file that ships with the module is written with `!module-path` instead.
